challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: She don't like coffee in the morning.
items.correction: She doesn't like coffee in the morning.
items.rule: Third person singular requires 'doesn't', not 'don't'.

items.sentence: They have been waiting for an hour.
items.rule: Present perfect continuous is correctly formed.

items.sentence: He goed to the store yesterday.
items.correction: He went to the store yesterday.
items.rule: 'Go' is irregular. Past tense is 'went', not 'goed'.

items.sentence: I am taller than my older brother.
items.rule: Comparative 'taller than' is correct for two people.

items.sentence: We was happy to see you at the party.
items.correction: We were happy to see you at the party.
items.rule: Plural subject 'we' requires 'were', not 'was'.

items.sentence: The children are playing outside right now.
items.rule: Present continuous with plural subject and 'are' is correct.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: If I was you, I would study harder.
items.correction: If I were you, I would study harder.
items.rule: Subjunctive mood requires 'were', not 'was' for hypotheticals.

items.sentence: Neither the teacher nor the students were late.
items.rule: With 'neither...nor', verb agrees with the nearest subject.

items.sentence: She has went to the library already.
items.correction: She has gone to the library already.
items.rule: Present perfect requires past participle 'gone', not past tense 'went'.

items.sentence: He asked me where I lived.
items.rule: Reported speech with backshift of tense is correct.

items.sentence: The news are very surprising today.
items.correction: The news is very surprising today.
items.rule: 'News' is an uncountable noun — always takes singular verb 'is'.

items.sentence: She speaks both French and German fluently.
items.rule: Correct use of 'both...and' with appropriate verb form.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: I have been living here since five years.
items.correction: I have been living here for five years.
items.rule: Use 'for' with duration and 'since' with a point in time.

items.sentence: She suggested that he take the early train.
items.rule: Subjunctive after 'suggest' correctly uses base form 'take'.

items.sentence: Me and my friend went to the cinema.
items.correction: My friend and I went to the cinema.
items.rule: Subject pronoun 'I' is correct; 'me' is object form. 'I' comes last.

items.sentence: The book which I borrowed was fascinating.
items.rule: Relative clause with 'which' for a thing is grammatically correct.

items.sentence: He made me to clean the entire kitchen.
items.correction: He made me clean the entire kitchen.
items.rule: 'Make' + object + bare infinitive (no 'to').

items.sentence: Had I known earlier, I would have helped you.
items.rule: Inverted third conditional is correctly formed.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: Each of the students have their own laptop.
items.correction: Each of the students has their own laptop.
items.rule: 'Each' is singular — requires 'has', not 'have'.

items.sentence: By the time we arrived, the movie had already started.
items.rule: Past perfect 'had started' correctly shows prior action.

items.sentence: She is more smarter than her classmates.
items.correction: She is smarter than her classmates.
items.rule: Double comparative: 'smarter' already includes comparison.

items.sentence: The teacher, along with her students, is attending the event.
items.rule: 'Along with' doesn't change subject — verb agrees with 'teacher' (singular).

items.sentence: I look forward to hear from you soon.
items.correction: I look forward to hearing from you soon.
items.rule: 'Look forward to' takes a gerund (-ing), not infinitive.

items.sentence: Were the assignment submitted on time?
items.correction: Was the assignment submitted on time?
items.rule: 'Assignment' is singular — requires 'was', not 'were'.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: He run very fast during the race yesterday.
items.correction: He ran very fast during the race yesterday.
items.rule: Past tense of 'run' is 'ran'.

items.sentence: The committee has reached a unanimous decision.
items.rule: Collective noun 'committee' with singular verb is correct.

items.sentence: There is many reasons to study English.
items.correction: There are many reasons to study English.
items.rule: 'Reasons' is plural — requires 'are', not 'is'.

items.sentence: She would rather walk than drive to work.
items.rule: 'Would rather' + base verb + 'than' + base verb is correct.

items.sentence: Despite of the rain, we continued the match.
items.correction: Despite the rain, we continued the match.
items.rule: 'Despite' doesn't take 'of'. Use 'in spite of' or 'despite' alone.

items.sentence: Not only does he speak English, but he also speaks Japanese.
items.rule: Correct correlative conjunction with subject-verb inversion.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: I wish I can speak more languages.
items.correction: I wish I could speak more languages.
items.rule: 'Wish' for present unreal situation takes 'could', not 'can'.

items.sentence: She has been working here since 2019.
items.rule: Present perfect continuous with 'since' + point in time is correct.

items.sentence: The team is consisted of twelve players.
items.correction: The team consists of twelve players.
items.rule: 'Consist of' is active voice — no passive 'is consisted of'.

items.sentence: Hardly had he arrived when the meeting started.
items.rule: Inverted sentence with 'hardly...when' is correct formal English.

items.sentence: She asked me that where I was going.
items.correction: She asked me where I was going.
items.rule: Indirect questions don't use 'that' before question words.

items.sentence: He is used to working late at night.
items.rule: 'Be used to' + gerund correctly means accustomed to.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: The furnitures in the office need to be replaced.
items.correction: The furniture in the office needs to be replaced.
items.rule: 'Furniture' is uncountable — no plural 's', singular verb.

items.sentence: It is essential that every student attend the orientation.
items.rule: Mandative subjunctive after 'essential that' uses base form 'attend'.

items.sentence: She speaks English very well, isn't she?
items.correction: She speaks English very well, doesn't she?
items.rule: Tag question must match the main verb — 'speaks' → 'doesn't she'.

items.sentence: The more you practise, the better you become.
items.rule: Correlative comparative 'the more...the better' is correct.

items.sentence: He suggested me to apply for the scholarship.
items.correction: He suggested that I apply for the scholarship.
items.rule: 'Suggest' takes a that-clause, not 'suggest someone to do'.

items.sentence: I would have called you if I had known your number.
items.rule: Third conditional is correctly formed.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: She enjoyed to play tennis after school.
items.correction: She enjoyed playing tennis after school.
items.rule: 'Enjoy' always takes a gerund (-ing), never infinitive.

items.sentence: He denied having stolen the documents.
items.rule: 'Deny' + gerund (perfect gerund here) is correct.

items.sentence: The informations provided were very helpful.
items.correction: The information provided was very helpful.
items.rule: 'Information' is uncountable — no plural, singular verb.

items.sentence: She needn't have worried about the exam.
items.rule: 'Needn't have' + past participle — unnecessary past action — is correct.

items.sentence: I am agree with your proposal completely.
items.correction: I agree with your proposal completely.
items.rule: 'Agree' is a verb, not an adjective — no 'am' before it.

items.sentence: Scarcely had the game begun when it started raining.
items.rule: Inverted sentence with 'scarcely...when' is correct formal usage.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: He has less friends than his brother.
items.correction: He has fewer friends than his brother.
items.rule: 'Friends' is countable — use 'fewer', not 'less'.

items.sentence: The teacher asked us to hand in our assignments.
items.rule: Phrasal verb 'hand in' used correctly with direct object.

items.sentence: She speaks English more better than before.
items.correction: She speaks English much better than before.
items.rule: Double comparative: 'better' is already comparative; use 'much better'.

items.sentence: Were I in your position, I would accept the offer.
items.rule: Inverted conditional with subjunctive 'were' is correct formal English.

items.sentence: The meeting will be holded in the conference room.
items.correction: The meeting will be held in the conference room.
items.rule: 'Hold' is irregular — past participle is 'held', not 'holded'.

items.sentence: She insisted on paying for everyone's dinner.
items.rule: 'Insist on' + gerund is the correct pattern.

challengeSets.instruction: Is each sentence grammatically CORRECT or WRONG?

items.sentence: They discussed about the new company policy.
items.correction: They discussed the new company policy.
items.rule: 'Discuss' is transitive — no preposition 'about' needed.

items.sentence: No sooner had she finished than the phone rang.
items.rule: 'No sooner...than' with past perfect inversion is correct.

items.sentence: I am boring with this lecture.
items.correction: I am bored with this lecture.
items.rule: Use 'bored' (feeling) not 'boring' (causing boredom) for the person.

items.sentence: The report must be submitted by Friday at the latest.
items.rule: Passive voice with modal 'must be' + past participle is correct.

items.sentence: She apologized for arrive late to the meeting.
items.correction: She apologized for arriving late to the meeting.
items.rule: Preposition 'for' takes a gerund (-ing), not base form.

items.sentence: Little did they know what was about to happen.
items.rule: Inverted sentence with negative adverb 'little' is correct.
